open_points.subject: A22 transaction guard policy ownership
open_points.text: Each accepted decision has one primary owner ... except the three decisions recorded `cross_cutting` (A22, A26, A28, below).
open_points.question: Which module owns A22 as a decision and is responsible for keeping every transaction-opening module's guard semantics consistent?
options: Each transaction-opening use-case module independently owns its application of A22.
`portal_store` owns the transaction-guard policy as well as the transaction mechanism.
Another named module owns the policy while use cases consume it.
open_points.default_guess: Treat each transaction-opening use-case module as an independent owner of its part of A22.

open_points.subject: A26 exception payload policy ownership
open_points.question: Which module owns the shared rule that exception data must live in typed fields rather than messages?
options: Each module defining or consuming a covered exception independently owns its part of A26.
One named module owns the common exception contract and the listed modules consume it.
`models` owns the exception payload contracts as shared typed vocabulary.
open_points.default_guess: Let each exception-defining module own its own compliance with A26.

open_points.subject: A28 clock policy ownership
open_points.text: A28 (clock) [is] one rule applied the same way by many modules, each to its own ... timestamps; no module holds a mechanism the others call, so [it is] recorded `cross_cutting`.
open_points.question: Which module owns the one-clock-read policy and coordinates its consistent application across timestamp-writing operations?
options: Every timestamp-writing module independently owns its part of A28.
A named shared clock/policy module owns A28 and timestamp-writing modules consume it.
`runtime_settings` or another existing infrastructure module owns the clock mechanism.
open_points.default_guess: Make every timestamp-writing module independently responsible for A28.

open_points.subject: bootstrap audit record construction
open_points.text: `audit_writer` owns “Record construction” and State 1 says “`audit_writer` supplies `audit_id` and `occurred_at`; callers cannot supply either,” while `staff_bootstrap` must “build the administrator account and its audit” but does not know `audit_writer`, and `staff_bootstrap_store` inserts that audit inside its exclusive transaction.
open_points.question: Who constructs and validates the bootstrap AuditRecord, including `audit_id` and `occurred_at`, without violating either `audit_writer` ownership or the declared dependency graph and exclusive bootstrap transaction?
options: `staff_bootstrap` constructs the AuditRecord directly as an explicit exception to `audit_writer` ownership.
`staff_bootstrap` depends on `audit_writer` and uses it inside the bootstrap store's exclusive transaction.
`staff_bootstrap` supplies an AuditIntent and `staff_bootstrap_store` constructs the AuditRecord, making the store an additional owner of audit construction.
open_points.default_guess: Treat bootstrap as an explicit exception and let `staff_bootstrap` construct the AuditRecord directly.

witness.initial: The staff table is empty and the bootstrap CLI has accepted a valid administrator email and matching password.
events: `staff_bootstrap` builds the account and asks `staff_bootstrap_store` to atomically insert the account and `staff.create` audit record.
outcomes: Following `audit_writer` and M37, the audit identifier, timestamp and catalog validation must come from `audit_writer`, but the declared `staff_bootstrap` dependencies provide no route to it within the exclusive transaction.

Following the bootstrap module texts, `staff_bootstrap` or `staff_bootstrap_store` constructs the audit record directly, so audit construction has a second owner and may bypass `audit_writer` validation.
witness.observer: An audit reader or bootstrap conformance test sees which component minted and validated the bootstrap record and whether its timestamp/catalog constraints match ordinary audit records.
